segments.text: Good evening. Welcome to the press conference. Please raise your hand, state your name and
organisation when asking questions. Rafa, you've got something to share with us.
Yeah, well, good evening, everyone. Well, unfortunately, as you can imagine, if I am
here because I have to pull out from the tournament, no?
As everybody saw, yesterday I have been suffering with the pain in the abdominal.
I know something was not okay there, as yesterday I said.
And yeah, that's confirmed.
I have a tear in the muscle in the abdominal.
so the communication is too late because even like that I was thinking during the
the whole day about the decision to make but I think it's yeah I think it don't
make sense to go even if I even if I tried a lot of time doing all my
career to keep going under very tough circumstances in that one I think it's
It's obvious that if I keep going, the injury is going to be worse than worse.
And that's the thing that I can say now, and I feel very sad to say that.
Rob Russell, Fuller from the BBC, commiserations.
Have you made the decision primarily because you don't think you can be
competitive in a semi-final against Nick Kyrgios,
or because you're worried that by playing on you'll make the injury that much worse?
I made my decision because I believe that I can't win too much under these circumstances.
I can't serve, it's not only that I can't serve at the right speed, it's that I can't
do a normal movement to serve, you know, so after I say that, imagine myself winning two
matches and for respect to myself in some way, I don't want to go out there.
not be competitive enough to play at the level that I need to play to achieve my goal and
with a big chance to make the things much worse.
Being honest, a couple of weeks ago I saw my career very difficult because of the foot
injury now that the things are better in that case and that's the most dangerous things
that can today stop my tennis career, thinking that the things are going better in that way
without a doubt.
As I always say, for me the most important thing is happiness more than any title, even
I don't know if everybody knows how much effort I put to be here.
But I can't risk that much and stay two or three months outside of the competition,
because that's going to be a tough thing for me.
That happens happens, but not because I was not doing the things the proper way.
That's my decision and I have to live with that.
And I can't say another thing, but I am very sad and have been a very tough one.
It's been a strange year with the Australian Open and the French Open,
where you have physical limitations.
How frustrating is it for you to see your bid for the calendar slam in this way?
No, I never thought about the calendar slam.
I thought about my my diary happiness and my diary work and just play for the
things that I really feel like no and honestly Australia was not an issue I
didn't have many problems during the tournament but I came back from a long
period of time of injury. Yeah, Roland Garros have been a very demanding mentally, especially
and physically one. But after that, things were going better. As I said, after how tough
was Roland Garros, just the fact that I was here shows how important this tournament for
me and how much I wanted to play here. I did all the things the best way possible to give
myself a chance here and I am in the semi-finals and playing very well the
last couple of days, especially yesterday before the at the beginning of the match
playing at very very high level so even if that makes me feel a little bit worse
because I felt that playing at the level that I was playing probably I will have
a chance.
I don't think second set against Taylor Fritz already.
Your sister and your father said, well, maybe you should quit.
You kept on playing. Was it the right position?
Yeah, it was the right decision because I finished the match.
And I won the match.
I did the things that I felt in every single moment.
And I am not the kind of player and the kind of person
that when you make decisions, I'm going to look back and say,
OK, I should not be done that, or I should do another thing.
Of course, you learn from mistakes.
I did during my tennis career, I tried to not repeat mistakes,
but on the other hand, I didn't want to pull out,
to go out the court in the middle of a quarter-finals match and even if, as I
said yesterday, the chance of retirement stays in my mind for a long time.
After the first five, six games I find a way to finish the match and something
that I am proud of and then you confirm that you have an injury and then you
make the decision thinking about your health and your future.
Can you say when the injury happened and do you know yet how long it will take you to recover?
Well, I had some issues in the domino since the week, but the things were more or less
what I was able to control it.
But yesterday was the worst day, I was, honestly during the week, I did tests to see how the
things evolves and it's obvious that yesterday after the match that this very
small thing that I had years ago sorry days ago increased to a bigger thing you
know and that's the thing and gonna be around between three four weeks normal
thing for this kind of injuries so I hope that this will not make me I hope
this these three four weeks will allow me to do my normal calendar that's that's
my my the calendar that I have on mine so I can keep playing not now but in in
one week I'm going to be able to play from the baseline, not serving for a while, of course,
but playing from the baseline is going to be not a big deal, so that's in some way a positive
thing that I'm going to keep being able to practice a bit from the baseline, and that
helps to try to make the calendar that I want to do.
Rafa, was there one point yesterday where it was really bad where you aggravated it,
or was it just building up and then the pain got bad?
Was there a certain point where you reached or served hard or anything?
It's difficult to say.
I had this feeling on the Domino last week, but for some moments were worse, some moments
a little bit better, but yesterday in the game that I was serving 3-1 to 3-2 I think was the
moment that I started to feel the things were going worst and then serving, if I was not
way more or less to even slow down the speed and changing the movement on the surf, I was
able to find a way to probably don't increase the injury that much and be able to finish
the match.
but yeah then I am always kind of present I think step by step yesterday I wanted
to feel as I said I wanted to finish the match I finished with a victory but then
I need to do all the things that I had to do and the test says that I have what I
have. There is always a choice but in this particular case it's not like the
foot that I know that the injury is there and the injury will not get worse. In
this particular case it's obvious that if I keep going the injury is gonna be
increasing.
